summary: A 300-foot concrete boiler exhaust stack next to the Unit 3 Power Block (the 2018 Draft EIR dates both to 1965; press reports give 1962 for the power plant); explicitly retained as an existing structure under the Design for Development, and proposed by the developer (May 2025) as a temporary art gallery within the interim Prequel Park.

milestones.text: Unit 3 Power Block and the Boiler Stack dated 1965 in the 2018 Draft EIR ('both constructed in 1965'), which extended the Third Street Industrial District's period of significance to 1965 and added both as contributing resources; the DEIR's project description gives 'ca. 1965', and press reports give 1962 for the power plant (see open questions)

Final Design for Development sets the Stack's height limit at its existing height, and provides that if the Stack collapses or is damaged beyond repair, the 300-ft height limit will not apply to a replacement and the land will instead be used as open space

Developer announces plans, with Heatherwick Studio, to open the Stack as a temporary art gallery as part of Prequel Park; the Chronicle reports the park, if approved, could open by the first quarter of 2027

The Boiler Stack and the adjoining Unit 3 Power Block (dated 1965 in the 2018 Draft EIR; press reports give 1962 for the power plant) are covered by the final Design for Development (Feb 26, 2020) as existing structures: Standard 6.2.1, 'Height of Existing Structures', sets the Stack's height limit at its existing height and provides that a collapsed or irreparably damaged Stack is not replaced by a new structure of that height

facts.value: 300 ft (described in the DEIR as a '300-foot tall concrete boiler exhaust stack'; the D4D final labels it 'EXISTING STRUCTURE (~300')' in Figure 6.2.3, and Standard 6.2.1 refers to its 300-foot height limit)

1965 in the 2018 Draft EIR (Table 4.D-1, 'Boiler Stack 1965'; section 4.D: 'both constructed in 1965'; project description, section 2.D.4: 'Boiler Stack (ca. 1965)'). Press reports give 1962 for the power plant (Chronicle, May 22, 2025: 'a remnant of the retired power plant built in 1962'; SF YIMBY, Oct 24, 2025: 'the retired 1962-built power plant'), and the final Design for Development captions a '1964 photo of Unit 3 and the Stack'; these are not reconciled (see open questions)

Contributor to the Third Street Industrial District (added when the district's period of significance was extended to 1965); the 2018 DEIR states the Boiler Stack is not considered to be individually significant

Retained as an 'Existing Structure' under the Design for Development; the height limit for the Stack is fixed at its existing height and does not carry over to a replacement structure if the Stack is destroyed

Proposed to be opened as a temporary art gallery within Prequel Park (developer, May 2025); ICA SF (Oct 28, 2025) says it will use the Stack as 'a vertical gallery' from 2027, and its exhibition page says 'Opening Fall 2027'

open_questions: The Stack's construction date differs between sources. The 2018 Draft EIR gives 1965 (Table 4.D-1, source line 'San Francisco Planning Department HRER, 2018', lists the Boiler Stack as 1965; section 4.D: 'both constructed in 1965'; project description, section 2.D.4: 'Boiler Stack (ca. 1965)'). The Chronicle (May 22, 2025) says 'a remnant of the retired power plant built in 1962' and SF YIMBY (Oct 24, 2025) says 'the retired 1962-built power plant'; neither gives the Stack's own year. The final Design for Development says PG&E added Unit 3 'in the 1960s' and captions a '1964 photo of Unit 3 and the Stack'. The DEIR says the Third Street Industrial District was documented in 2008 with a period of significance ending in 1958, and that the 2018 historic resource evaluation extended it to 1965, adding the Stack and Unit 3. This dossier gives the DEIR's date as the DEIR's and does not choose between the sources.

ICA SF's press release (Oct 28, 2025) says it will launch a public art initiative at 'The Stack at Prequel Park' in 2027, turning the Stack into 'a vertical gallery', and its exhibition page says 'Opening Fall 2027'. The Port Commission memo (Nov 14, 2025) says the Planning Department issued a temporary use authorization for Prequel Park in June 2025 and that the developer hopes to open the park in the first quarter of 2027 (page 2) or the third quarter of 2027 (page 4). No source says whether that authorization covers opening the Stack itself to visitors. The DataSF building-permit applications for Prequel Park (202512051053, 202512051066, 202512081182) were all 'filed' with no issued date in the data read on 2026-10-12, and none of their descriptions mentions the Stack.

Structural condition: the 2018 Draft EIR (Mitigation Measure M-CR-5e) says a preservation plan 'shall include stabilization of the Boiler Stack prior to construction' only 'If deemed necessary upon further condition assessment of the resource'; no condition assessment was found. Ownership: the DEIR describes the Power Station sub-area as 'currently owned by the project sponsor' but does not say which lot holds the Stack, and no source read says who owns the Stack's parcel today. Landmark status: the DEIR says the Stack is a contributor to the Third Street Industrial District and 'is not considered to be individually significant'; no source read shows an individual landmark designation.
